note: textual.py's trigram guard: 1287 -> 1286. Char/Text.condition_to_sql admits `isinstance(value, COLLECTION_TYPES) and all(isinstance(v, str) ...)` for the whole set ("in", "like", "ilike", "=like", "=ilike"), then hands `value` to pattern_to_translated_trigram_pattern on the non-"in" branch, which does regex work and raises TypeError on a list. Measured: pattern_to_translated_trigram_pattern(['abc','def']) -> "TypeError: expected string or bytes-like object, got 'list'". It is nevertheless unreachable, and the guard rather than the caller is what makes it so: the domain is optimized before it reaches SQL, and optimizations._optimize_like_str coerces any non-str, non-SQL like-operand to str(value) -- or, for =like/=ilike, raises "The pattern to match must be a string". Verified on test_orm.indexed_translation (Text, translate=True, index="trigram"), where Domain([("name","like",["hello","world"])]).optimize(model) yields ("name","like","['hello', 'world']"): a str, matching nothing, no crash. So an assert states the invariant at the point the code depends on it, which is the shape Many2many._relation_columns already uses here. NOT counted in this move: service/model.py:64, the other finding the 2.3.0 bump surfaced. get_public_method does `elif method is not None and per_class.get(name) is method: return method` and mypy reports Callable|None on the return; reveal_type confirms it does not narrow, and it still does not when rewritten to bind the cached value first, nor with a nested `if cached is not None:` -- it reports "Any | None" either way. Rewriting it changed nothing measurable, so it was reverted rather than left as churn. That one error stays in this floor.
